\section*{Question 3}

The figure above shows the graph of the piecewise-linear function \(f\). For \(-4 \leq x \leq 12\), the function \(g\) is defined by
\[
g(x)=\int_{2}^{x} f(t) d t
\]
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] Does \(g\) have a relative minimum, a relative maximum, or neither at \(x=10\) ? Justify your answer.
\item[(b)] Does the graph of \(g\) have a point of inflection at \(x=4\) ? Justify your answer.
\item[(c)] Find the absolute minimum value and the absolute maximum value of \(g\) on the interval \(-4 \leq x \leq 12\). Justify your answers.
\item[(d)] For \(-4 \leq x \leq 12\), find all intervals for which \(g(x) \leq 0\).
\item[(a)] The function \(g\) has neither a relative minimum nor a relative maximum at \(x=10\) since \(g^{\prime}(x)=f(x)\) and \(f(x) \leq 0\) for \(8 \leq x \leq 12\).
\item[(b)] The graph of \(g\) has a point of inflection at \(x=4\) since \(g^{\prime}(x)=f(x)\) is increasing for \(2 \leq x \leq 4\) and decreasing for \(4 \leq x \leq 8\).
\item[(c)] \(g^{\prime}(x)=f(x)\) changes sign only at \(x=-2\) and \(x=6\).

\begin{tabular}[t]{|l|l|}
\hline \(x\) & \(g(x)\) \\
\hline -4 & -4 \\
\hline -2 & -8 \\
\hline 6 & 8 \\
\hline 12 & -4 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}
On the interval \(-4 \leq x \leq 12\), the absolute minimum value is \(g(-2)=-8\) and the absolute maximum value is \(g(6)=8\).
\item[(d)] \(g(x) \leq 0\) for \(-4 \leq x \leq 2\) and \(10 \leq x \leq 12\).
\item[] \(1: g^{\prime}(x)=f(x)\) in (a), (b), (c), or (d)
